🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Computer Organization - Memory Hierarchy

A computer system has a 64 KB, 4-way set-associative cache with a block size of 32 bytes. The processor generates 32-bit byte-addressable physical memory addresses. How many bits are there in the Tag field of each address?

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
Cache size = $64\text{ KB} = 2^{16}$ bytes.
Block size = $32\text{ bytes} = 2^5$ bytes $\implies$ Block Offset = 5 bits.
Number of cache lines = $\frac{64\text{ KB}}{32\text{ B}} = 2^{11} = 2048$ lines.
With 4-way set associativity, number of sets = $\frac{2048}{4} = 512 = 2^9$ sets $\implies$ Set Index = 9 bits.
Address length = 32 bits.
Tag bits $= 32 - (\text{Set Index} + \text{Block Offset}) = 32 - (9 + 5) = 32 - 14 = 18$ bits.

🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Computer Organization - Pipelining

A 5-stage instruction pipeline has an ideal CPI of 1. Branch instructions constitute 20% of the instruction mix. Conditional branches are resolved in the 3rd stage (causing a 2-cycle penalty on misprediction). A dynamic branch predictor is used with a prediction accuracy of 85%. Assuming no other pipeline stalls, what is the effective CPI of this processor? (Round to 2 decimal places).

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
Branch frequency = 0.20.
Misprediction rate $= 1 - 0.85 = 0.15$.
Penalty per mispredicted branch = 2 cycles.
Stall cycles per instruction $= 0.20 \times 0.15 \times 2 = 0.06$ cycles.
Effective CPI $= \text{Ideal CPI} + \text{Stalls} = 1 + 0.06 = 1.06$.
